Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start the security/ops signoff for our Redwood private deployment, the engineering team has asked for a short, focused review of the Infrastructure-as-Code surface we'll be shipping into our VPC. We want to avoid the big monolith modules and instead move to a smaller, composable set of artifacts that our ops team can own and patch.

High-level asks from our side:
- A concise list of Terraform modules that will be applied in our account (networking, peering, k8s bootstrap, storage)
- Helm charts and the values we expect customers to reconcile vs. overwrite in their namespace
- Ansible roles (or other configuration) used for node-level setup and service registration
- CI/CD gating: what checks you run (tfsec, tflint, yamllint, helm unit tests), how rollbacks are triggered, and test harnesses for canary deploys
- Networking constraints: IP ranges, recommended subnet sizing, cross-account peering patterns, and any required BGP or MGMT plane routing

I've attached a short diff that enumerates the modules we've seen so far and a checklist the compliance team will use for signoff. Can we do a 45-minute call to walk these items and align on a minimal path to production? Prefer Wed or Thu this week (any time after 10am PT).

Thanks,
Jacob

Jacob — appreciate the clear list. Happy to run through everything. Quick notes before the call so we can be efficient:

1) Terraform modules: we intentionally split networking (vpc, subnets, route tables), peering (cross-account role + peering resource), control-plane bootstrap (k8s control plane + autoscaler IAM), and storage (EBS/CSI config + backup CRs) into separate modules. We'll provide a module manifest that maps module name -> variables that require customer input.

2) Helm: our recommended approach is "values-as-override" where we ship opinionated defaults but expose a small set of knobs (replica counts, CPU/memory caps, metrics endpoints). We will not put secrets in chart values; secret references expect customer KMS.

3) Ansible: used only for initial node tuning (sysctl, kernel modules, NVMe config) in on-prem/hybrid setups. The roles are idempotent and live in a separate repo we version with tags that CI will reference.

4) CI gating: we run a multi-stage pipeline — lint -> static analysis (tfsec/tflint)-> unit tests for helm (chart-testing) -> integration smoke in ephemeral infra. Rollbacks are automated via canary controller with webhook triggers, and we snapshot terraform state before apply for emergency rollbacks. We will share the pipeline YAML and the small test harness we use internally.

5) Networking: we'll send a recommended IP allocation table and required peering flow. For on-prem via VPN, we recommend a /16 split with customer-controlled subnets; for direct cloud-peering we have documented route-map examples. If you have strict egress controls we can support dedicated egress gateways.

Proposed time: Thu 2027-06-17 10:30am PT (45m). I'll invite Laura and Aditya to run the deep-dive on modules and CI respectively.

- 10m: Inventory of IaC artifacts (Marcus / Laura)

- 10m: Networking and peering patterns (Marissa / Jacob)
- 10m: Acceptance criteria for signoff and next steps

I'll attach the CI gating proposal and an initial manifest in the follow-up.

— Marcus Lin
